lines.text: While I was being chased, half drowned and insulted in the south, Greyhollow carried on without me. Bram wrote me four letters about that autumn, each exactly one page. Tobin wrote eleven, with drawings.
Bram's first order was a wall. A real one, all the way round the village, twice as high as a man.
Slower! Groan a bit! Somebody might be watching!
Granny carried a boulder up the ladder on her hip. Bram made her carry it back down, and do it again, looking tired.
Rook, Birk and Tarn supervised. That is, they stole the masons' lunches, dug under the new wall faster than anyone could build it, and followed Bram everywhere he went.
Absolutely not. Go away. ...Fine. One of you can sit there. Not you. ...Fine.
Then Tobin built a bellows.
My grandfather's book wants a fire hotter than any forge in the kingdom. Everyone says that's impossible. So I'm building impossible bellows.
Will they explode?
Almost certainly not.
They exploded on the Tuesday.
Nobody was hurt. Three goats were found two fields away, upside down, and very calm. Tobin was delighted. He said it meant the fire was hot enough.
Meanwhile, Kell was learning to bargain. Pell had left him a list of prices and one piece of advice. Never say the first number.
Forty crowns a lamp, my good Skeld. My final offer. A very generous one.
Kell said nothing. Kell said nothing for a very long time.
...Sixty? Seventy! Seventy, and you stop looking at me like that!
The Skeld do not bargain. We wait.
That's not bargaining.
It is working.

On the ninth day, a woman and a little girl walked in from the midlands, with a note in my handwriting. Bram pretended to be very annoyed. Then he gave them the room over the bakery. The warmest in the village.
That child hasn't stopped talking since she got here. Not for one minute. I like her.
And every night, when the hall was empty, Bram went and stood under the lamp. Tobin heard him once, through the wall. He told me years later, when it no longer mattered who knew.
He's gone south, my lady. Right into their house. He has your eyes, and your song, and not the faintest idea.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy, coming soon.
